SCF: An R Package for Analyzing the Survey of Consumer Finances

The SCF package simplifies analysis of the U.S. Federal Reserve’s Survey of Consumer Finances—a triennial, nationally representative dataset with multiple imputation and complex survey design. The package includes tools for downloading, transforming, visualizing, and modeling SCF microdata.

📦 Features

🔽 Download & Load Data

  • scf_download(): Download and flatten SCF microdata by year.
  • scf_load(): Load as a svyimputationList survey object.

🔧 Data Wrangling

  • scf_update(): Add or recode variables across implicates.
  • scf_subset(): Subset multiply-imputed data consistently.
  • scf_implicates(): Extract implicate-level results.
  • scf_MIcombine(): Rubin-style pooling of estimates.

📊 Descriptive Analysis

  • scf_mean(), scf_median(), scf_percentile(): Weighted summary stats
  • scf_corr(): Correlation with significance tests
  • scf_xtab(): Weighted cross-tabulations

📈 Regression & Modeling

  • scf_ols(): Linear regression with Rubin’s Rules
  • scf_logit(): Logistic regression with pooled fit stats
  • scf_glm(): Generalized linear models (e.g., binomial, Poisson)

🎨 Visualization

  • scf_plot_dbar(): Univariate bar chart (categorical)
  • scf_plot_bbar(): Bivariate bar chart (discrete × discrete)
  • scf_plot_cbar(): Summary of continuous by group (e.g., mean, median)
  • scf_plot_hist(): Histogram of continuous variable
  • scf_plot_scatter(): Scatterplot for two continuous variables

🔧 Installation 

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("jncohen/scf")

🚀 Getting Started 

library(scf)

# Download & load SCF 2022
scf_download(2022)
scf2022 <- scf_load(2022)

# Add new variable
scf2022 <- scf_update(scf2022, senior = age >= 65)

# Estimate mean net worth by education
scf_mean(scf2022, ~networth, by = ~edcl)

# Plot distribution of education
scf_plot_dbar(scf2022, ~edcl)

# Run linear regression
scf_ols(scf2022, networth ~ income + factor(edcl))
